items.title: Ray Bauduc Interview, 1984-06-27
items.q: I mean, we, we, we used to play with, with Bill, uh, Eastwood. Bill Eastwood on banjo.

ctx.x: Well, I mean, he, he, he would be able to tell you more about it, see. Or, Bill Eastwood. Yeah, I knew him too. Because they, they lived over there in Al Jays, you know, I mean, uh, Eastwood and, and they played, uh, with, uh, well, he played at the halfway house when I was there, see. But, uh, but Emmett, uh, they went on, uh, on a tour. He, I don't, uh, Johnny Frisco drummed up, let's see if I can remember this guy. Johnny Frisco was on drums, Santo, Emmett Hardy, and, uh, I don't know, Harry Shields or Larry…

items.title: Ray Bauduc Interview, 1984-06-26
items.q: And then later on, I played with Eastwood out at, with Abby Brunson and the guys at the halfway house.

ctx.x: He was a trained teacher as a matter of fact.
Yeah. Well Emmett Hardy came there. He was studying machinists. And then Bill played out the halfway house with him. Bill Eastwood. Mm-hmm. They were both from Al Jays, you know.
